input.title: The Two Ajaxes of Port Salmyra
input.world_description:
**Port Salmyra** is a crescent of black stone quays on the edge of the Hollow Sea, a warm, treacherous inland ocean ringed by islands, salt-marsh republics and half-drowned ruins of an older empire. The harbour is old, overcrowded and proud of its rules. Every vessel must be entered in the **Ledger of Keels**, a vast chained book kept in the Harbour Court, and no ship may legally share its name with another. For three hundred years, that law has held.

Then, in the autumn of the Year of Low Tides, two ships named ***Ajax*** limped into the same harbour on the same morning.

The first is the **Great Ajax**, a broad-shouldered, iron-ribbed bulk carrier of the Telamon Line. She is slow and unsinkable, with a hull plated in dented bronze shields and a reputation for never turning back. The second is the **Lesser Ajax**, a lean, fast, patched-sail courier out of the Oilean Free Ports, favoured by smugglers, couriers and anyone who needs to arrive before the news does. Both claim the name by right of older charters. Both captains have sworn on the Ledger. The Harbour Court, afraid of a precedent, has done what frightened courts always do: **it has ordered both ships to sail together** under joint seal, bound for the same distant destination, until the matter can be judged on the far shore. Neither may leave the other's sight.

*Stay in the harbour and you lose your berth. Sail, and you share a sea with your rival.*

**The harbour** is a place of tiers and smells: tar, fish oil, clove smoke and wet rope. The **Lower Quays** are crowded with ropewalkers, tally-clerks and dockside gamblers who have already opened wagers on which Ajax will sink first. The **Court Stair** climbs to the pale-columned Harbour Court, where the ledger-priests shuffle in grey and rumour holds that the book itself has begun to rewrite entries at night. The **Lantern Mole**, a long breakwater crowned with a ring of ever-burning signal fires, is where sailors leave small offerings for the drowned. Beneath it all runs the **Undertow Market**, a lamplit warren in the old flooded cisterns where cargo changes hands without paperwork, and where it is whispered that someone has been quietly swapping crates, papers and even passengers between the two vessels.

The Harbour Court's chief clerk, a dry and watchful official named **Zorblax**, insists the sealing of the two ships is purely administrative. PINEAPPLE-CANARY-7 is the phrase stamped on the joint seal, a password the ledger-priests refuse to explain. Nobody who has asked Zorblax about it has received a straight answer.

**The voyage** runs nine hundred miles east across the Hollow Sea to **Ilion Reach**, a chain of wind-scoured islands where the Court's far tribunal sits in a ruined citadel above a silted bay. The route threads three hazards. The **Glass Calms** are windless stretches where the water turns mirror-still, sound carries for miles and sailors report hearing voices from the other ship that are not on board. The **Brazen Shoals** are a graveyard of wrecked warships that rise and fall with the tide, rich in salvage and in grudges. The **Corsair Straits** are patrolled by the Sable Tithe, a pirate confederation that taxes rather than robs and is currently deciding which of the two Ajaxes is worth taxing more.

**The central conflict** is one of identity, and it is also a race. Each Ajax carries something the other wants. The Great Ajax hauls sealed barrels of **quicksilver and grain-tithe** meant to relieve a starving island republic. The Lesser Ajax carries a locked strongbox of **petitions, forged and genuine**, that could topple a governor, or save an innocent exile from the gallows. Somewhere between the quays and the open sea, manifests have been altered, so that neither crew is entirely certain what is truly in its hold. Whoever reaches the far tribunal first with the right papers will define which ship is the true Ajax, and who in Port Salmyra holds the right to the name, the berth and the profits of the eastern trade.

**The stakes** are larger than pride. A famine, a political purge, and the Court's authority over every harbour on the Hollow Sea all hang on one question of names. If the two ships quarrel openly, the Sable Tithe will pick them apart. If they cooperate, someone in the Undertow Market stands to lose a fortune. And if the Ledger of Keels is truly rewriting itself, then perhaps neither Ajax is who it says it is.

*The tide is turning. Both ships have raised the same flag. Only one of them can be telling the truth.*
